description: A university research lab can make two types of diabetes medicine, medicine A and medicine B. Per dose, medicine A takes 30 units of imported material and 50 units of mRNA to make. Per dose, medicine B takes 40 units of imported material and 30 units of mRNA to take. The lab has available at most 300 units of imported material and 400 units of mRNA. The lab can make at most 5 doses of medicine A and the number of doses of medicine B must be larger than the number of dosed of medicine A. If one dose of medicine A can treat 12 people and one dose of medicine B can treat 8 people, how many doses of each should be made to maximize the number of people that can be treated?

ImportedMaterialPerDoseA.definition: Amount of imported material required to produce one dose of medicine A

MRNAPerDoseA.definition: Amount of mRNA required to produce one dose of medicine A

ImportedMaterialPerDoseB.definition: Amount of imported material required to produce one dose of medicine B

MRNAPerDoseB.definition: Amount of mRNA required to produce one dose of medicine B

MaxImportedMaterial.definition: Maximum available units of imported material

MaxDosesA.definition: Maximum number of doses of medicine A that can be produced

TreatmentPerDoseA.definition: Number of people treated by one dose of medicine A

TreatmentPerDoseB.definition: Number of people treated by one dose of medicine B

objective.description: "Maximize the total number of people that can be treated by producing doses of medicine A and medicine B."
